title: Sleep & Recovery Assessment
purpose: Evaluates sleep duration, schedule regularity, subjective sleep quality, and academic disruption to sleep.
description: Helps students assess whether their sleep habits provide adequate physiological and cognitive recovery between demanding lecture and lab days.
target_population: Students observing irregular bedtimes or daytime sleepiness
instructions: Answer the following questions based on your typical sleep patterns over the last 14 days. These questions are for your personal reflection.
source: Calma Educational Prototype - Circadian Rhythm & Sleep Pacing Module.
validation_status: Educational self-reflection questionnaire; not a clinical sleep diagnostic.
disclaimer: This questionnaire is not an evaluation for insomnia, sleep apnea, or medical sleep disorders. If you experience persistent sleep disruption, consult campus health services.

scoring.type: Descriptive metrics and feature mapping for sleep_hours
scoring.interpretation: 7 to 9 hours of nightly sleep is the recommended guideline for university students. Sleeping fewer than 6 hours regularly is strongly correlated with increased study exhaustion.

questions.text: On average, how many hours of sleep do you get per night?
How would you rate the overall quality of your sleep?
How refreshed and alert do you typically feel within 30 minutes of waking up?
How consistent are your bedtimes and wake times throughout the week?
options: Highly erratic (bedtime shifts by more than 3 hours)
Somewhat variable depending on assignment deadlines
Consistent on weekdays, shifting on weekends
Very consistent (bedtime varies by less than 1 hour every day)

questions.text: How often does academic anxiety or deadline worry keep you awake when trying to fall asleep?
Do you feel you have sufficient downtime outside of academic responsibilities to unwind before going to sleep?
options: No downtime (study right until turning off lights)
